newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Primedia buys Interleisure firms.
newsitem.headline: Primedia buys Interleisure firms.

text.p: South African media and communications group Primedia Ltd said on Tuesday that it had bought various businesses in Interleisure Ltd for 1.5 billion rand.

Primedia said in a statement that the purchase price was equal to 7.92 rand per Interleisure share and was being financed through a combination of cash, debt and Primedia units. It was payable in September.
The firms that Primedia has bought are:
- a 100 percent stake in cinema group Ster-Kinekor Theatres;
- 100 percent of Ster-Kinekor Pictures which holds distribution rights for leading U.S. movie firms;
- Interleisure's 85 percent stake in Ster-Kinekor Home Entertainment, a video rental and retail distribution business;
- 100 percent of Cinemark, the country's only cinema advertising placement organisation; and
- 30 percent of an international venture to establish a cinema circuit in Europe.
The group said that analysts expect Primedia's group turnover to approach one billion rand for the year ending June 1998 and profit before debenture interest and tax in excess of 225 million rand.
The acquisition was expected to have a material impact on Primedia's earnings for the year to June 1997, the group said.
It said that its strategy was to develop an integrated entertainment group with interests across media platforms ranging from film and television to games and music.
William Kirsh, Primedia's chief executive officer, estimated the integrated entertainment industry outside of radio broadcasting was worth seven billion rand.

"...Primedia has minimal exposure to this industry. The acquisition of the Interleisure businesses acquired significantly alters the profile and positions us to exploit the enormous growth that we anticipate from this industry in the future," Kirsh said.
Primedia said that black empowerment groups will own up to 15 percent of the businesses bought, spearheaded by Cape-based black empowerment grouping Siphumelele Investments.
